summary: Cross-cloud role assumption failing due to session-tag truncation on assume-role chain
description:
Issue summary: Deployments to Dedicated cluster in prod are blocked because the infra provisioning pipeline cannot obtain cross-account credentials for the GPU fleet. Impact: New dedicated node pools could not be created; rolling deploys were delayed ~3 hours for a single customer onboarding. Environment: prod (aws us-east-1) using GCP CI runner (us-west1) that federates to AWS via workload-identity and STS assume-role chain.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger infra provisioning pipeline from GCP CI (service account A).
2) Pipeline exchanges workload-identity token for AWS STS credentials via our identity-broker (assume-role-with-web-identity).
3) Broker then calls AssumeRole to target account role with session tags.
4) Observe failure in the broker logs and pipeline stops.

Observed behavior:
- Broker logs show repeated failures: "AccessDenied: SessionTags cannot be larger than allowed size" and "AssumeRole chain rejected: Tag truncated -> role condition failed".
- The infra task fails with exit code 2 and error: "Failed to assume target-role: AccessDenied".
- Affected runs show 100% failure for jobs that request more than 2 session tags.

Expected behavior:
- Broker should successfully exchange identity token and assume target account role, propagating necessary session tags (team, ci-run-id, env) so audit/AWS condition checks succeed.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- broker stderr: "ERROR: sts:TagLengthExceeded: session tag payload length exceeded 2048 bytes"
- pipeline output: "aws:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed: InvalidIdentityToken" (followed by tag-related message in broker)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ava Morgan: Initial report — provisioning pipeline started failing at 09:04. Attached broker logs and pipeline job id job-2026-03-10-0901.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Diego Patel: I can reproduce from staging runner. Broker returns tag length errors when we include 4+ session tags; looks like the broker concatenates metadata into a single tag string before calling AssumeRole. Opening a deep-dive.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Priya Singh (SRE): Observed that AWS denies sessions where the total serialized tag payload exceeds ~2k bytes. Our tag generation started including long git refs and user-agent strings after a recent agent change (see infra PR).

2026-03-11 08:27 - Diego Patel: Quick mitigation deployed to identity-broker: trim optional tags (git_ref, run_metadata) and enforce per-tag length limits. Re-ran pipeline jobs in staging: provisioning succeeded. Preparing prod rollout and Terraform fix to avoid reintroducing long tags.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Diego Patel: Prod rollout completed at 11:00. Verified three successful dedicated node pools created. Closing after monitoring 24h.
2026-03-12 11:10 - Ava Morgan: Confirmed customer onboarding continued; raising follow-up task to update runbook and add unit tests for tag serialization.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Broker concatenates tags into one serialized payload that exceeds AWS session tag size limit -> confirmed by reproducer.

Hypothesis 2: Recent change in infra agent started including full commit message and long branch names -> traced to infra agent v2.4.1 (commit 8f3a12) which appended full run context into 'ci_metadata' tag.

Findings: AWS enforces combined tag payload limits and also truncates tags in the assume-role chain; our role condition required exact tag equality which failed after truncation. Affected flow: GCP OIDC -> identity-broker -> AssumeRole -> AssumeRole (target account).
Related risk: If tag truncation occurs silently, role-based conditions may deny sessions leading to intermittent access failures for automation.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to identity-broker: stop serializing run_context as a single tag; instead send compact tags (team, ci_run_id, environment) and strip long fields. Release: identity-broker v1.7.2.
Terraform change: add validations to pipeline that reject job metadata containing fields longer than 256 chars before kicking the broker. PR: infra/pull/4987 merged and deployed to staging/prod.
IAM change: relaxed exact-string conditions on target role trust policy to allow prefix matching for ci_run_id and added CloudWatch alarm for STS:TagLengthExceeded errors. PR: iam/pull/212.
Post-action verification: three consecutive provisioning runs in prod succeeded; monitoring shows no further STS tag errors.
